en: The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Twelve Names of the Great Auspicious Goddess, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of the Tang Dynasty.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Bhagavat was dwelling in the world of Sukhāvatī, together with [an assembly of]...
A great multitude of bodhisattvas surrounded him on all sides as he preached the Dharma.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, headed by the Great Auspicious Goddess (Mahāśrī-devī),
all rose from their seats, approached the World-Honored One,
prostrated with their heads at his feet, and each sat to one side.
At that time, the Blessed One, desiring to benefit all sentient beings who were of meager merit and impoverished,
addressed the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
saying: "Noble son, if there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, or any other classes of sentient beings..."
Whoever knows these twelve names of the Great Auspicious Goddess,
and is able to receive, uphold, recite, study, practice, and make offerings to them, and explains them for others,
will be able to eliminate all karmic obstacles of poverty.
They shall attain great wealth and nobility, with abundant riches and treasures.
At that time, the assembly of devas, nāgas,
and the eight classes of beings spoke with one voice, saying:
As the World-Honored One has spoken, it is true and not false.
We wish to hear the twelve names;
we pray that the World-Honored One, out of great compassion, will expound them for us.

The Buddha said: "Listen well, and I shall now speak for you. These are the twelve names: Auspicious, Auspicious Lotus, Adorned, Endowed with Wealth, White, Great Renown, Lotus-Eyed, Great Radiance, Giver of Food, Giver of Drink, Jewel Light, and Great Good Fortune."
"You should receive and uphold this.
I shall now further recite the Great Auspicious Dhāraṇī, which says:
Tadyathā | Śrīṇi śrīṇi | Sarvakārya-sādhanī | Sini sini | Ṇi ṇi ṇi ṇi | Ālokistha-nāśaya svāhā. At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken this dhāraṇī, [said:]...
He addressed the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"This Great Auspicious Dhāraṇī and its twelve names are capable of eliminating poverty and all inauspiciousness."
All aspirations shall be fulfilled.
If one can recite this sutra three times during each of the three periods of the day and night,
or constantly uphold it without interruption.
With a mind intent on benefiting others, one should reverently make offerings according to one's ability to the Bodhisattva Mahāśrīdevī;
thus, one will swiftly obtain all manner of abundant wealth, prosperity, auspiciousness, and peace.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
along with the great assembly of devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of supernatural beings,
heard from the Buddha the exposition of the twelve names and the dhāraṇī.

They marveled that such a thing had never occurred before. All were filled with great joy, and having received it with faith, they practiced accordingly. Thus ends the *Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Twelve Names of the Goddess Mahāśrī*.
